 REA: Reverse Engineer Anything

 One MCP for reverse engineering across binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.

 See a feature you like. Understand how it works, down to the binary level. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Website · Guides · Showcases 

 

Quick start · Showcases · How REA works · What you can analyze · Build RL environments · FAQ · Documentation

 npx rea-agents setup 

 

 [!IMPORTANT]
 Get REA from morluto/rea,
 rea.tools, or the rea-agents npm package.
 Follow the installation and release links from these official sources. A similar
 repository name or copied README does not establish that a download is official.

 

 

 

 

 
 
 
 
 
 Join the Reverse Engineering Community 
 
 Discord · Q&A · Show and Tell 
 
 
 

 

 

---

See a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project.

REA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion.

Setup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine.

 Showcases

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 DX-Ball: reconstruct a sound-pan calculation 
 Recover a position-to-pan helper from x86 instructions and verify the C reconstruction against 3,205 original-x86 cases and all 63 compiled function bytes. 
 Read the case study ·
 Reconstruction repository 
 
 
 
 
 Notion: trace the Electron clipboard bridge 
 Follow the renderer’s clipboard API through preload and IPC into the main process to see how Notion handles rich clipboard data. 
 Read the case study 
 
 
 
 
 TH04: recover a DOS bullet-ring calculation 
 Recover fixed and aimed angle calculations from the PC-98 game’s 16-bit instructions and compare the reconstructed C++ with historical compiler output. 
 Read the case study ·
 Reconstruction repository 
 
 
 
 

If you've used REA on something interesting, we'd love to see it. Share your
case in an issue or a
pull request, including the target,
your question, how REA helped, and what you found.

 How REA works

Your agent uses REA through MCP to inspect a target and trace the relevant code.
It can use the evidence REA returns to ask follow-up questions, explain behavior,
or build and test an implementation. The CLI uses the same workflows.

 

Open the full-size figure.

 

 What you can analyze

REA covers native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, websites, .NET
assemblies, Android apps, firmware, and recorded runtime and network activity.

Supported targets and requirements

 

For native decompilation, choose a provider that supports your target format
and host OS. See choosing a deep analysis provider.

 Build RL environments

Build a local environment from a recorded web session or a Linux desktop app
so an agent can practice a task and check its result.
Build an RL environment with REA.

 FAQ

 
 Which agents can use REA? 

Any agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the
supported agents; other clients can use
manual MCP registration.

 

 
 Do I need a native analysis engine? 

Deep native analysis uses Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna, depending on the target
and operation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native
analysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra, IDA and Kuna
use your existing installations. See provider setup
for the options and their supported targets.

 

 
 Do I need to start Hopper first? 

REA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may
ask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the
same user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open
Hopper manually if needed. See
Hopper startup and troubleshooting.

 

 
 What does installing the skill from skills.sh do? 

The skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent.

install.html:
Get started at rea.tools for step-by-step instructions by operating system, agent, and analysis provider.

Connect your agent (MCP)

With Node.js and npm installed, run this from a trusted directory outside the project you plan to analyze.

npx rea-agents setup

Choose your agent, review and approve the setup plan, then restart your agent. Setup backs up existing configuration and adds REA's MCP connection and investigation skill. See the installation guide for supported clients, plugins, manual registration, and troubleshooting.

Try asking your agent:

Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a
similar feature for my project.

Replace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand.

Use REA from the terminal (CLI)

Inspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR:

npx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json

The result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence. Replace the path with your target, such as "D:/apps/example" on Windows.

To install the rea command for regular use:

npm install --global rea-agents
rea --help

For native analysis, configure a provider first. The CLI and Evidence guide covers provider selection, native commands, snapshots, and scripting. For Linux prerequisites, see the installation guide.

Update REA

For a global npm or Bun installation, run the updater and follow its setup instructions.

rea update

If you use npx, refresh your agent setup with:

npx rea-agents@latest setup

Review the setup changes and restart your agent. See update and uninstall instructions for package runner options and troubleshooting.
